artworks.title: Hylas and the Nymphs
artworks.description: Waterhouse's Manchester canvas is the modern image of Hylas: the Argonaut youth kneels at a dark pool while seven water-nymphs rise to draw him under. Painted in 1896 for the Pre-Raphaelite twilight of Victorian myth, it freezes Theocritus' Mysian spring — beauty as a trap, Heracles' beloved vanishing into water. The painting remains the single most familiar depiction of the abduction that left the Argo without its strongest hero.

artworks.title: Hylas and the Water Nymphs
artworks.description: Thorvaldsen's neoclassical marble relief (Thorvaldsens Museum, Copenhagen) turns the rape of Hylas into a cool frieze of grasping nymphs and a yielding youth. Where Waterhouse would later drown the scene in foliage and pond-light, the Danish sculptor keeps the myth as pure outline — the Argonaut cupbearer pulled from the shore by desire. It is the academic afterlife of Apollonius' Mysian episode, carved for a Europe that read Hylas as both beauty and loss.

artworks.title: Hylas Carried Off by Nymphs
artworks.description: Henry Howard's British Romantic canvas stages the moment the naiads lift Hylas from the spring — limbs entangled, pitcher forgotten, the Argonaut already halfway into another world. The painting belongs to the same nineteenth-century fascination with Theocritus' Idyll XIII that later fed Waterhouse: Hylas as the beautiful youth whom water and love erase from the Argo's crew.

films.title: Jason and the Argonauts
films.description: Harryhausen's adventure keeps the Argonaut voyage for a mass audience — the mythic company that once included Hylas before the Mysian spring took him from Heracles.

popCulture.title: Idyll XIII (Hylas)
popCulture.creator: Theocritus
popCulture.description: Theocritus' pastoral tells how the naiads stole Hylas at the spring — the Hellenistic poem that fixed the Argonaut's disappearance as a love-story of water and echo.
